excerpt: Romei et al. applied rhythmic TMS at 10 Hz, 20 Hz, or 5 Hz to occipital and parietal regions while participants reported near-threshold visual stimuli. TMS at 10 Hz impaired visual detection contralateral to stimulation, improved detection ipsilateral to stimulation, subsided within 3 s, and produced no comparable detection effects at 5 or 20 Hz.
overview: The frequency-specific TMS result gives the review a causal line of evidence. If driving alpha-range activity selectively impairs contralateral perception while neighboring frequencies do not, alpha is more plausibly a suppressive mechanism than a passive correlate of attention state.
title: Ten Hertz TMS Suppression
